title: Updates
blurb: Updates failing, stuck, or asking to restart.

remedies.title: Which version of Windows or macOS do I have?
remedies.why: IT and app makers ask for the exact version and build.

steps.text: Settings › System › About shows edition, version (e.g. 24H2) and OS build. Or run winver.
Apple menu › About This Mac shows the macOS name and version.

remedies.title: Upgrade to the latest Windows or macOS version
remedies.why: Big yearly versions bring new features and keep security support going.

steps.text: Settings › Windows Update: the feature update appears when your PC is ready. Check compatibility with PC Health Check.
Software Update offers the new macOS when your Mac supports it.
Back up first and keep the computer plugged in.

remedies.escalate: Work computers: IT controls the timing; ask before upgrading.

remedies.title: Update drivers safely
remedies.why: Drivers from Windows Update or the PC maker are tested; "driver updater" apps often cause trouble.

steps.text: Windows Update › Advanced options › Optional updates › Driver updates.
Or the PC maker's own tool (Dell Command Update, Lenovo Vantage, HP Support Assistant).
If a new driver causes trouble, roll it back in Device Manager.

remedies.title: "Not enough space" to install an update
remedies.why: Updates need room to download and unpack, often 10–30 GB.

steps.text: Free up space with DeskMedic's Cleanup (includes old update files).
See what's big in the Disk map.
Windows can use a USB drive for extra room during the update when it asks.

remedies.title: Pause or delay updates for a while
remedies.why: You can delay updates for a short time, for example before a presentation.

steps.text: Settings › Windows Update › Pause updates (up to a few weeks).
Software Update › Automatic updates (i): turn off automatic install for now.
Don't leave updates off for long; they carry security fixes.

remedies.escalate: Work devices may not allow pausing.
